item: Background job follow-ups: store swaps, resume counts, setup stops, vLLM reasons (Lane E list a-e, R689 job side)
key_paths: src/jobs/llm_bulk_queue.py; src/api/llm.py; src/api/insights.py; src/safety/panic.py; src/database/repair.py; src/llm/concurrency.py; src/llm/vllm_lifecycle.py
summary: (a) The panic wipe and the repair swap move the settings store's swap epoch before they replace the file too, so a bulk-queue save read from the old file is refused instead of landing in the new one. (b) A resumed run counts as its own stored only as many earlier results as it had counted before the stop; a result another run wrote during the pause counts as skipped. (c) The queue's generation is read inside _next under the same lock. (d) A test makes a save wait behind hold_writes while the epoch moves. (e) The superseded /api/insights/reindex stands back (busy) while the backlog job runs. Also: the stop is looked at right after the run's machine probe and after the selection, and the model resolves on the backend already probed (one probe, not two); a Resume pressed while a stopped drain ends is kept (unless the app is shutting down); the streamed POST /api/llm/bulk polls its task-manager Stop during a generation; run_concurrent uses daemon worker threads, so an abandoned vLLM generation no longer holds the process at exit; vLLM lifecycle answers carry fixed phrases instead of exception text (CodeQL class). Tests: tests/test_shutdown_stop_deadline.py, tests/test_store_swap_epoch_followups.py, tests/test_llm_concurrency.py.
